method_note: Chose claims on repo metadata, release dates, data-model constraints, code paths a test oracle would use, legal citations (ESPR, Batteries Regulation, Implementing Regulation 2026/1778), registry user guide statements, Zenodo versions and licences, GS1 link-type list, Have Your Say status, DOIs and engine-mapping statements. Primary sources re-read this session: gh api (GitHub), Zenodo API, Crossref API, Cellar legal texts (ESPR via local pdftotext of the Cellar PDF; 2026/1778 and 2023/1542 via fetch tool), registry user guide and GS1 in Europe paper via local pdftotext, GS1 ref.gs1.org, brpapi, and the engine source tree. The D3.2, D4.1 and redirection-report passages (section numbers, option details) were not re-read in full; they are listed as not_confirmed only where a claim depends on them and was listed.

checked.claim: URI Syntax states the domain is not part of the GS1 identifier; sections 2, 4.9, 4.11, 4.12, 5; canonical form id.gs1.org
checked.evidence: Section 4.12 does require id.gs1.org for canonical URIs; sections 5.1 and 4.11 show non-canonical custom-domain URIs and the same keys under several domains. A fetch of the first 100000 characters did not find an explicit sentence that the domain is not part of the identifier; the fetch tool may have missed it. Section 3.1 (hostname) and 5.1 are the relevant places.
checked.correction: Cite section 4.12 (canonical form) and 5.1 (custom-domain examples) for the point; avoid saying the standard states the domain is 'not part of' the identifier unless the exact section is located.

checked.claim: Implementing Regulation 2026/1778 Art. 8(7)(e): Commission checks, where relevant, the link to the back-up; Art. 8(9)(c) provider reference; recital 16; Art. 3(f)
checked.evidence: Act of 16 July 2026, OJ 17 July 2026. Art. 8(7)(e) is an automatic check at submission that the back-up link is valid; Art. 8(9)(c) stores a provider reference where relevant; Art. 8(9)(d) stores integrity as evidence; Art. 3(f) reference list of verified providers; recital 16 says automated checks do not prove compliance.

checked.correction: Optionally add that Art. 15(3) allows unannounced suspension.

checked.correction: Say: the registry has a registration form with Batteries pre-selected at item level, but v1.03 states that successful registration is not yet possible (semantic catalogue pending). This also strengthens the file's own inference about why no back-up input is visible.

rule5_findings.problem: Records the ISO/IEC numbers 19875 and 18975 as cited inside D4.1. The numbers sit next to a note about an inconsistency, which comes close to commenting on the content of protected documents. 18975 also appears in a sentence about the GS1 paper (source new-gs1-in-europe-enabling-dpp-v2-2) in the same way.
rule5_findings.fix: Keep as bibliographic pointers only; reword to 'D4.1 uses two different ISO/IEC numbers for one block; not resolved (protected)' without describing what either document covers.

rule5_findings.problem: 'D4.1 says its lifecycle API should follow the CEN-CENELEC JTC 24 specification' and the registry guide pointer 'URL format compliant with JTC 24 standards' state what project documents say about protected standards; they only name them, so this is acceptable.
States that chapters 4.3 and 6 'restate a protected standard' from a prior record. That characterises the content of a protected document indirectly.
rule5_findings.fix: Reword to 'chapters 4.3 and 6 were not used (prior record flagged them as referring to a protected standard)'.

missed_items.topic: Registry cannot yet accept battery passports
missed_items.fact: The user guide v1.03 says successful registration of battery passports is not currently possible because the semantic catalogue or content for the group is not yet defined. This explains the absence of a back-up input and means the Art. 8(7)(e) check cannot be seen in practice yet.
The act says the Commission checks that the back-up link is valid, where relevant. The file says the method is not described; the word 'valid' is the only criterion given.

missed_items.topic: Registry user guide UPI error list
missed_items.fact: The guide names a separate 'UPI URL is invalid' error for bad format, unsupported protocol, disallowed domain or non-permitted port, distinct from the technical error for excessive redirects or a less secure redirect.
Art. 15(2) availability is stated to be subject to paragraph 3, which allows unannounced suspensions; relevant to any availability oracle for the registry.
infrastructure/interfaces.py already defines too_many_redirects and redirect_out_of_scope fault names, so redirect-chain fixtures partly exist for identifier.resolve.

overall: The file is largely reliable on repository facts, Zenodo versions, licences, DOIs, the GS1 link-type list, the Have Your Say status and the legal citations I re-read (ESPR, Batteries Art. 78, Implementing Regulation 2026/1778); 24 of 29 checked claims were confirmed. Two errors matter: the 7.0.0 folder commit hash and date mix up the parent folder with the 7.0.0 folder, and the statement that the official registry is live for battery registrations contradicts the user guide, which says successful registration is not yet possible. The GS1 URI Syntax claim about the domain not being part of the identifier is not located verbatim. Engine-mapping statements checked against the source tree are accurate, with the redirect-limit mapping only partly supported. The D3.2 and D4.1 section-level details were not re-read and remain unverified here. Rule 5 exposure is small and limited to ISO/IEC numbers and indirect remarks about protected documents.
